glosses: to get to know, acquaint oneself with
Se lier d’amitié, se familiariser avec quelqu’un ou avec quelque chose.

examples.text: Avant cette époque, il n’avait jamais entendu parler de guerre, ou s’il en avait entendu parler, ce mot n’évoquait en lui aucune image, ne s’accointait en sa cervelle à aucune notion précise.
Il s’accointa de cette Larentia et l'aime tellement qu'il la laissa son héritière.
Mes enfants, accointez-vous, nous allons de ce pas à l’église où nous attend le curé.
Il s’est accointé d’un homme de fort mauvaise compagnie.
Combien de fois l’avait-il accointée au cours de cette nuit ?

glosses: Serrer quelqu'un de près, dans les coins.

examples.text: Il ne put aller plus loin, car elle le poussa dehors. Mais il revint à la charge les jours suivants. Il trouvait moyen de l’accointer dans la grange, dans le quéreux, même dans la maison ; et, plus d’une fois, elle se réjouit d’être assez forte pour ne rien craindre d’un pauvre gars comme lui.

glosses: To furnish or give experimental knowledge of; to make (one) know; to make familiar.

examples.text: I think you should acquaint him with the realities of the situation.
He is despised and reiected of men, a man of sorrows, and acquainted with griefe: and we hid as it were our faces from him; hee was despised, and wee esteemed him not.

Before a Man can be in any capacity to ſpeak on any ſubject, 'tis neceſsary to be acquainted with it: Or elſe 'tis as fooliſh to ſet him to diſcourſe on it, as to ſet a blind Man to talk of Colours, or a deaf man of Muſick.

glosses: To communicate notice to; to inform; let know.

examples.text: Acquaint her here, of my Sonne Paris Loue,

I muſt acquaint you, that I haue recciu'd
New-dated Letters from Northumberland:

I had almoſt forgotten to acquaint your honor, that one major Alford (who was in mr. Love's conſpiracy) was of the graund inqueſt at Saliſbury, and was very zealous in his highneſſe ſervice here, and his good affection and wiſe carriage here, did much advantage the buſſineſe.
He went directly, sign'd the indentures, was put into the ship, and came over, never writing a line to acquaint his friends what was become of him.

October 2 1642, Isaac Basire, letter to John Evelyn
What success it may further have I shall acquaint you at my coming over
[I]f you have skimmed through even a paragraph of my poor neglected little magnum opus you will know I am unusually acquaint with my inner workings.
